newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA SAYS HANDSETS BOOSTED Q1 EARNINGS.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA SAYS HANDSETS BOOSTED Q1 EARNINGS.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said on Tuesday healthy profitability at its mobile phone division boosted group earnings in the first quarter this year after a slight loss in Q1, 1996.
Nokia reported first-quarter group operating profit up 186 percent at 1.46 billion markka, and profit before tax and minorities rose to 1.45 billion markka from 399 million.
"The increase in Nokia's operating profit was mainly attributable to the significant improvement in the operating profit of Nokia Mobile Phones," Nokia said in a statment.
"The business group recorded a healthy profitability level, compared to a slight operating loss in the first quarter of 1996," it said.
Nokia's infrastructure arm Nokia Telecommunications' first-quarter net sales rose 34 percent to 3.73 billion markka.
"Nokia Telecommunications also reported higher profits than in he comparable period a year ago," it said, calling the results strong.
In other operations, first-quarter net sales rose to 1.63 billion markka from 1.50 billion, up 8.7 percent, but excluding structural changes, net sales growth was 53 percent, Nokia said.
"Operating profit of other operations was also higher than in the first quarter of 1996," it said.
Nokia said positive operating cash-flow had boosted its financial position further.
"At the end of March, the net debt-to-equity ratio was -18 percent compared to -9 percent at the end of 1996," it said.
Capital expenditure in January-March totalled 507 million markka, up from 471 million in the year-ago period, Nokia said.
